pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP) THE SMOKING GUN: The oxidation of excreted porphobilinogen (PBG) into porphobilin turning the urine a port-wine hue upon light exposure, accompanied by devastating motor paralysis triggered by CYP450-inducing anticonvulsants (phenytoin and carbamazepine). PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Acute Intermittent Porphyria is an autosomal dominant inborn error of heme biosynthesis caused by a partial deficiency of hydroxymethylbilane synthase (HMBS), also known as porphobilinogen deaminase (PBGD). When exposed to triggers such as fasting, hormonal changes, or CYP450-inducing drugs, hepatic ALAS1 is dramatically upregulated. Due to the enzymatic bottleneck, intermediate neurotoxic metabolites (delta-aminolevulinic acid and porphobilinogen) accumulate massively, precipitating autonomic instability, psychiatric manifestations, hypothalamic dysfunction causing SIADH (severe hyponatremia), and rapid axonal motor neuropathy. Administration of hemin and glucose halts ALAS1 transcription to arrest the attack.
